approach: Each pair of the three sources produces its own beat, and adding those gives the beats produced, while the ear only tells apart the distinct loud pulses it actually hears.

steps.text: List the beat frequency from every pair of the three sources.
The number of beats produced per second is the sum of the beats from all three pairs acting together.
steps.why_this_step: Each pair of waves independently goes through its own cycle of reinforcing and cancelling, and all three cycles run at once.

steps.text: Adding the three waves gives a resultant whose loudness rises to a strong peak once every second and to a much weaker peak once every second, with true silence occurring twice every second.
steps.why_this_step: Writing the sum this way shows the loudness envelope has exactly 2 points of complete silence per second, so a listener hears exactly 2 distinct pulses of loudness per second.

steps.text: State the number of beats heard per second.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the two 1 Hz beats from the neighbouring pairs are the same beat and only counting 2 beats produced, ignoring that the third pair also contributes at 2 Hz.
Swapping the two numbers and reporting 2 produced and 4 heard.
